paper.title: Improved Regret Bounds for Online Fair Division with Bandit Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Online fair division with unknown means subject to proportionality in expectation (normalized values)
unmapped: Actions are fractional allocations X in R^{n x m} (columns sum to 1) of items to n players; item type k_t drawn uniformly from m types each round; only the value of the allocated player for the item is observed
Reward is linear: <X, mu*>_F; regret against best proportional allocation Y^{mu*}
Proportionality-in-expectation constraints X_i . mu*_i >= 1/n must hold at every round with high probability (constraints depend on the unknown means)
Values normalized: each player's means sum to 1; means lie in known [a,b] with a>0
Learner knows n, m, a, b
settings.definition_quote: Design an algorithm ALG such that the following result holds for any known n,m, T,a,b. Suppose that the true mean values satisfy a <= mu*_{ik} <= b for all i in [n],k in [m]. Then with probability 1-1/T, ALG will both satisfy the proportionality in expectation constraints for mu* and have regret for mu* of O~(sqrt T).

settings.name_in_paper: Online fair division with unknown means subject to general linear fairness constraints satisfying Properties A.2-A.5
unmapped: Fractional allocations of n players x m item types, random item types, observe only allocated player's value
General mean-dependent linear constraints <B_l(mu*), X> >= c_l satisfied by UAR, with continuity, slack and Lipschitz properties; must hold every round w.h.p.
Learner knows n, m, a, b, the constraint family and constants C_P3 and K
settings.definition_quote: We consider sets of fairness constraints {(B_l(mu*), c_l)}_{l=1}^{L} ... An algorithm ALG that uses allocation X^t at time t satisfies these constraints if <B_l(mu*), X^t>_F >= c_l for all t.

settings.name_in_paper: Online fair division subject to envy-freeness in expectation with normalized values (lower bound)
unmapped: Envy-freeness in expectation constraints (X_t)_i . mu*_i >= max_{i'} (X_t)_{i'} . mu*_i must hold every round w.h.p.
Normalized values (rows sum to 1), means in [a,b] with a=1,b=40 (as stated, before normalization)
settings.definition_quote: An algorithm ALG that uses fractional allocation X^t at time t satisfies envy-freeness in expectation if for all t < T and all i in [n], (X_t)_i . mu*_i >= max_{i'} (X_t)_{i'} . mu*_i.

conditions: 0 < a <= mu*_{ik} <= b for known a,b

source.label: thm:sqrtT_regret
source.quote: Suppose $n,m, T, a,b$ are known and that the true mean values satisfy $0 < a \le \mu^*_{ik} \le b$ for all $i \in [n]$, $k \in [m]$. With probability $1-1/T$, Algorithm \ref{algo:UCB} will both satisfy the proportionality in expectation constraints for $\mu^*$ and have regret for $\mu^*$ of $\tilde{O}(n^5m^3\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Holds with probability 1-1/T, jointly with constraint satisfaction at every round. Comparator is the best proportional allocation Y^{mu*}; mapped to best_policy. Runtime stated exponential in n and m. Õ hides dependence on a,b (C_P3 = bn/a). Proof uses 'sufficiently large T'.

symbols.K_c: Lipschitz constant K of constraint matrices B_l in mu (Property A.5)
symbols.C_P4: continuity constant of optimal welfare (Property A.4)

conditions: constraints satisfy Properties A.2 (satisfied by UAR), A.3, A.4, A.5

source.label: lemma:general_sqrtT_regret
source.quote: Suppose $\left\{\{(B_\ell(\mu), c_\ell)\}_{\ell=1}^{L}\right\}_{\mu \in [a,b]^{n \times m}}$ satisfy Properties ... Then with probability $1-1/T$, Algorithm \ref{algo:UCB} satisfies the constraints $\{(B_\ell(\mu^*), c_\ell)\}_{\ell=1}^{L}$ and has regret of $\tilde{O}(KC_{\mathrm{P}4} C_{\mathrm{P}3}n^3m^3\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Statement refers to Algorithm 1 but the general version is Algorithm 2 (Fair UCB). Property numbers resolved from printed labels (A.3 = fairness_to_UAR2_app, A.4 = continuous_app). Compute: paper says the second round of optimization makes runtime exponential.

conditions: a = 1, b = 40, n = 3, m = 3 (as in proof)
algorithm must satisfy envy-freeness in expectation constraints

source.label: thm:lower_bounds
source.quote: There exists $a,b,n,m$ such that no algorithm can, for all $\mu^* \in [a,b]^{n \times m}$ with rows that add to $1$, both satisfy the envy-freeness in expectation constraints and achieve regret of less than $\frac{T^{2/3}}{\log(T)}$ with probability at least $1-1/T$.

results.notes: Impossibility statement: no algorithm can simultaneously satisfy EF-in-expectation and have regret < T^{2/3}/log T with probability >= 1-1/T for all normalized instances. Recorded as an exact lower-bound threshold; the paper describes it as Omega~(T^{2/3}).
